args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 (which was also unhealthy as v2.3.1-rc in staging), health checks failed in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and the error rate was about 18%. checkout-api was rolled back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service reports healthy with about a 0.2% error rate. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

- **Problem:** v2.3.1, the latest deploy, was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. It was failing health checks with an error rate of about 18%. The release candidate for this version (v2.3.1-rc) had also been unhealthy in staging.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. I rolled back to it, and all three regions now run v2.3.0. A fresh status check shows the service is healthy, with the error rate down to about 0.2%. This didn't need change-manager approval because v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production.
- **Incident:** I opened INC-0001 as a SEV2 for checkout-api, which paged the on-call engineer. It describes the failure, the rollback and the recovery. It also says the cause of the v2.3.1 failure needs to be found before v2.3.1 is deployed again.
